arxiv-2102-09780.title: A Deep Graph Wavelet Convolutional Neural Network for Semi-supervised Node Classification
arxiv-2102-09780.creator: Jingyi Wang 1 , Zhidong Deng 2
arxiv-2102-09780.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jingyi Wang 1 , Zhidong Deng 2. Graph convolutional neural network provides good solutions for node classification and other tasks with non-Euclidean data. There are several graph convolutional models that attempt to develop deep networks but do not cause serious over-smoothing at the same time. Considering that the wavelet transform generally has a stronger ability to extract useful information than the Fourier transform, we propose a new deep graph wavelet convolutional network (DeepGWC) for semi-supervised node classification tasks.

arxiv-2104-11602.title: A new topological perspective of expanding space-times with applications to cosmology
arxiv-2104-11602.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . We discuss the possible role of the Tietze extension theorem in providing a rigorous topological base to the expanding space-time in cosmology. A simple toy model has been introduced to show the analogy between the topological extension from a circle S S to the whole space M M and the cosmic expansion from a non-zero volume to the whole space-time in non-singular cosmological models.

arxiv-2202-02250.title: Tighter Constraints of Multipartite Systems in terms of General Quantum Correlations
arxiv-2202-02250.creator: Jin-Hong Hao, Ya-Ya Ren, Qiao-Qiao Lv, Zhi-Xi Wang, Shao-Ming Fei
arxiv-2202-02250.description: Abstract Abstract Monogamy and polygamy relations characterize the quantum correlation distributions among multipartite quantum systems. We investigate the monogamy and polygamy relations satisfied by measures of general quantum correlation. By using the Hamming weight, we derive new monogamy and polygamy inequalities satisfied by the β \beta -th power and the α \alpha -th power of general quantum correlations, respectively.

arxiv-2208-12648.title: On the dependence of conditions in the linear mapping definition
arxiv-2208-12648.creator: Aslanbek Naziev 1
arxiv-2208-12648.description: Abstract . We study the (in)dependence of additivity and homogeneity conditions in the definition of linear mappings between vector spaces over the same scalar field. Unlike other works on the subject, dealing with particular fields like real or complex numbers, or with particular mappings like continuous or measurable, we consider the general case. This enables us to obtain complete picture.

arxiv-2211-04645.title: Quantum-critical scaling at the Bose-glass transition of the 3d diluted Heisenberg antiferromagnet in a field
arxiv-2211-04645.creator: Yuchen Fan, Rong Yu, Tommaso Roscilde
arxiv-2211-04645.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuchen Fan, Rong Yu, Tommaso Roscilde. The nature of the superfluid-to-Bose-glass (SF-BG) quantum phase transition, occurring in systems of interacting bosons immersed in a disordered environment, remains elusive. One fundamental open question is whether or not the transition obeys conventional scaling at quantum critical points (QCPs): this scaling would lock the value of the crossover exponent ϕ \phi – dictating the vanishing of the superfluid critical temperature upon approaching the QCP – to the value of quantum critical exponents for the ground-state transition.

arxiv-2305-13849.creator: Aishwarya Venkataramanan 1, 2, 3] Assia Benbihi 4 Martin Laviale 1, 3] Cédric Pradalier 2, 3]
arxiv-2305-13849.description: Abstract Recent works show that the data distribution in a network’s latent space is useful for estimating classification uncertainty and detecting Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) samples. To obtain a well-regularized latent space that is conducive for uncertainty estimation, existing methods bring in significant changes to model architectures and training procedures.

arxiv-2401-08752.title: Gravitational Raman Scattering in Effective Field Theory: a Scalar Tidal Matching at 𝒪 ⁡ ( G 3 ) \mathcal{O}(G^{3})
arxiv-2401-08752.creator: Mikhail M. Ivanov, Yue-Zhou Li, Julio Parra-Martinez, Zihan Zhou
arxiv-2401-08752.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mikhail M. Ivanov, Yue-Zhou Li, Julio Parra-Martinez, Zihan Zhou. We present a framework to compute amplitudes for the gravitational analog of the Raman process, a quasi-elastic scattering of waves off compact objects, in worldline effective field theory (EFT). As an example, we calculate third post-Minkowskian (PM) order ( 𝒪 ⁡ ( G 3 ) \mathcal{O}(G^{3}) ), or two-loop, phase shifts for the scattering of a massless scalar field including all tidal effects and dissipation.

arxiv-2402-12969.description: Abstract Significant strides have been made in natural language tasks, largely attributed to the emergence of powerful large language models (LLMs). These models, pre-trained on extensive and diverse corpora, have become increasingly capable of comprehending the intricacies of language. Despite the abundance of LLMs for many high-resource languages, the availability of such models remains limited for European Portuguese.

arxiv-2507-18127.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Inverse Design of Metasurfaces for Tailored Narrow Band Absorption
arxiv-2507-18127.creator: Sreeraj Rajan Warrier, Jayasri Dontabhaktuni
arxiv-2507-18127.description: Abstract The inverse design of metasurfaces poses a considerable challenge because of the intricate interdependencies that exist between structural characteristics and electromagnetic responses. Traditional optimization methods require significant computational resources and frequently do not produce the most effective solutions. This study presents a hybrid quantum-classical machine learning approach known as Latent Style-based Quantum GAN (LaSt-QGAN).

arxiv-2509-04739.title: Cavity QED based on strongly localized modes: exponentially enhancing single-atom cooperativity
arxiv-2509-04739.creator: Qian Bin, Ying Wu, Jin-Hua Gao, Aixi Chen, Franco Nori, Xin-You Lü

Here, we propose to exponentially enhance the single-atom cooperativity parameter by exploiting the strongly localized effect of modes in cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) systems.
